texts: Cotton of every field goes into the furnace alike, and comes out as the same glowing ember; who then is high, who low?
doha pls: cotton from any field burns the same in the furnace, so why do we call each other high and low
cotton, furnace, no castes
At the mill where I work, the owner's son and the sweeper's son both fainted in the furnace heat during the cotton drying, and the same doctor treated both; I'd love a doha on that.
I want a doha saying that all people, rich and poor, upper and lower, are like cotton from the same field, and when the furnace of life reaches them there is no difference in how they burn.
Every drop in the ocean is kin to every other; no wave is higher in the eyes of the deep.
doha plz: every stream ends up in the ocean, so there's no high and low among people
ocean, one humanity
My neighbour looks down on our family because we are poor, but at the beach last summer his child and mine played in the same ocean and neither could tell whose waves were whose; write a doha.

Compose a doha explaining that just as every stream, clear or muddy, joins the ocean and becomes one with it, all human beings return to the same Maker, so none should be proud or look down on another.
The salt of the king's table and the salt of the pauper's bowl was gathered from the same waters.
Write a doha that says the same salt seasons the food of the rich and the poor, and the same Creator made both, so those who boast of birth or wealth have forgotten how alike they are at their root.
salt, same for all
doha pls: salt for the rich and the poor is the same salt, so why the pride
At my cousin's wedding, the cook used the same salt for the guests' plates and for the servants' plates, and I thought how silly it is that we still sit at separate tables; please write a doha.
Whether a mark is drawn on the forehead of the priestly or the labourer, the same breath moves beneath it.

Please craft a couplet that says a mark on the forehead or a sacred string on the shoulder does not raise one man above another, because the Maker looks at the heart and sees every person as the same.
forehead mark, no castes
My upper-caste friend wears a forehead mark and refuses to eat with our family, though when his father was sick it was my father who gave blood; I would like a doha for him.
doha pls: the forehead mark doesn't make you better than anyone, we all come from the same source
Write a doha saying that in the forest, when thirst comes, the tongue of the rich and poor long for the same drop, and no one asks the caste or name of the one who brings the water.
We got lost in a forest on a trek, and the tribal guide who showed us the way shared his water with a banker and a student alike, never once asking who they were; please write a doha about it.
doha pls: in the forest all animals drink the same water and no tongue asks about caste
tongue, forest, one humanity
In the forest every tongue thirsts alike, and the same stream quenches the proud and the lowly.
I want a doha saying that humans are all made of the same breath and the same light, and that titles, wealth and birth are names we ourselves invent and the Maker never recognises them.
At the hospital, when my child was born, I saw a rich woman and a poor woman crying out in the same pain and holding the same newborn joy; make a doha out of what I felt.
doha idea: everyone is the same in front of the Creator
all are equal
The Maker looks upon the lord and the labourer with the same loving eye; why then do we divide?
I saw a skeleton in a school lab and the teacher said you cannot tell from it who was rich or poor, which struck me deeply; please write a doha.
doha pls: a skeleton doesn't tell you caste or wealth, think about that
Strip away the skin and the silk, and the skeleton smiles the same smile for king and sweeper alike.
Compose a doha that says if you look at the bones of a rich man and a poor man there is nothing to tell them apart, so what cause has anyone to be proud of birth or wealth?
skeleton, no distinction
no high, no low
From one source we all came, to one source we go; who then can stand above another?
My grandfather was a clerk and my grandmother a farmer's daughter, and they raised us to touch every elder's feet without asking their background; write a doha in their spirit.
Make me a doha that says every human being is born the same way, cries the same first cry, and feels the same hunger and love, so the walls of caste are made by men, not by the Maker.
doha pls: stop dividing people into high and low, it's all the same human
The needle stitches silk and sackcloth alike, and the chakor loves its distant beloved without asking who is watching.

Compose a doha saying that a needle does not ask whether it is sewing a prince's robe or a pauper's shirt, and so a wise soul sees with the chakor's single-hearted love, finding no difference between persons.
chakor, needle, same maker
The old tailor in our village stitched for the landlord and the labourer with the same needle and the same care, and said the chakor's love was as blind to rank; write a doha.
doha plz: even the chakor and a needle don't care who owns them, and God doesn't care who we are, all equal
The pot of water gives its coolness to the lord and the lowly, and the cotton warms both without question.
pot of water, cotton
doha pls: a pot of water is the same for everyone, the thirsty doesn't ask whose pot, cotton is the same too
At the village fair, a pot of water at the stall was given to all who passed, and a cotton seller sold to everyone at the same price whether they were rich or poor; write a doha.

Compose a doha that says the pot of water placed on the roadside quenches the thirst of the high-born and the low-born alike, and cotton covers every body without choosing, teaching us to give without discrimination.
Can you make a doha that says the bier is the last bed of the lord and the labourer, and once the heron-like silence of the cremation falls, no one remembers the caste or rank people were proud of.
The bier waits for the proud and the humble alike, and the heron stands at the water's edge, watching all pass.
Both the minister's father and the sweeper's father were carried on the same kind of bier when they died, and it was the same heron-white sky above both, I noticed; write a doha.
bier, heron, same end
doha: a bier carries everyone, the rich and poor, even a heron would see no difference
thorn, no caste
The thorn pricks the prince's foot and the pauper's foot with the same pain; pain knows no rank.
doha pls: a thorn hurts the rich and poor in the same way, we all feel pain the same
A thorn went into my friend's foot on a trip, and the village boy and the city boy cried out in the same words and bled the same red; write a doha about it.
Please write a doha showing that a thorn wounds the rich and poor equally, the blood and the pain are the same, and so we should treat each other with the same care and not with the pride of rank.
To the yogi's eye the lord and the labourer are one, as salt is one in every dish.
A yogi who lived on our street shared his salt and his roti with the poor and the rich, saying nobody's hunger was different from another's; please write a doha.
yogi, salt, all equal
Write a doha that says a true yogi sees no division between high and low, as the salt that seasons a king's meal also seasons a servant's, and the one who sees this has seen the Maker.
doha pls: a yogi sees everyone as the same, just like salt is the same in any food
doha pls: the winnowing fan separates grain from chaff, not rich from poor, God sees our hearts only
The winnowing fan parts the husk from the grain, never the high-born from the low; the chakor looks at the sky alone.
chakor, winnowing fan, no pride
Pen a doha that says the winnowing fan sifts by worth and not by birth, since the husk of pride flies away in the wind and only the grain of a pure heart stays behind for the Maker's eyes.
At harvest I watched my grandmother use the winnowing fan and said only the chaff flies away, not the poor and the rich as men believe; make a doha out of it.
one family of humans
Please write a doha for children saying that all of us are brothers and sisters from one source, that no one is born better than another, and that those who believe otherwise are mistaken.
One source has made all hearts; he who calls another low forgets his own origin.
doha idea: everyone's equal, no one's better
My daughter came back from school and asked why some kids won't sit with others, and I did not know what to say; I need a doha for her.

Compose a doha showing that the net of time catches everyone in the same way, whether he wears a crown or rags, and so those who think themselves higher than others should think of the rain that falls equally.
The fisherman's net and the king's treasure net were both washed by the same rain, and the rainbird sang without choosing whom to sing for; write a doha about this.
The rainbird drinks only the sky's gift, and the net of fate falls on all, king and commoner alike.
net, rainbird, same fate
doha pls: the net of fate catches everyone, rich or poor, and the rainbird drinks the same rain as everyone
My mother gave a handful of salt to our neighbour whose family is of a lower caste, and when others objected, she said salt does not ask whose kitchen it goes to; please write a doha.
doha: the salt is the same on a rich man's plate and a poor man's, so is the person
The salt dissolves into the soup of the rich and the poor with the same silence; so do we dissolve into the Maker.
salt, one humanity
I want a doha that says salt from the same lake sits on the tables of the great and the small, and the bodies that eat it are made of the same stuff, so rank is no cause for pride.
doha pls: sand doesn't care who walks on it and every tongue speaks the same truth at the end
The sand on the beach holds the footprints of a rich tourist and a poor vendor, and the waves wash both away; the tongue of time, I thought, speaks the same to all. Write a doha.
tongue, sand, no rank
Compose a doha that says the sand under the feet of kings and paupers is the same, and the tongue that speaks of rank will be silenced in the end by the same dust, so speak kindly.
The sand keeps no record of the proud, and the tongue of time speaks the same to all.
The blind man cannot see rank, and milk is white in every cup; only our pride paints the colours.

Please write a doha that says the blind man who cannot see rank treats everyone alike, as milk is offered to all children without question, and the sighted should learn this from him and rid their eyes of pride.
blind man, milk, same god
My blind grandfather never knew who was high or low in the village; he greeted all with the same warmth, and gave milk to every child, and I want a doha to honour him.
doha pls: a blind man can't see caste, he only knows people by their touch and voice, and milk is white for everyone
The musk deer's fragrance perfumes the poor man's path as much as the king's garden; the goodness of a soul has no rank.
I'd like a doha that says the musk deer's scent is not stronger near a mansion and not weaker near a hut, and a person's worth is in himself, not in the family of his birth.
The poorest woman in our village carries a fragrance of kindness that none of the rich ladies has, and I wanted a doha to say that value is not in birth.
musk deer, no rank
doha: a musk deer's scent is the same wherever it goes, in a mansion or in a hut
Born of one creation, we are kin; the ones who forget it have lost their way.
At the festival, I saw children from all castes playing together, and it was the elders who had to tell them to stop; write a doha.
I want a doha that says look with the same eye on a prince and a servant, a scholar and a labourer, a rich woman and a poor one, because the Maker made them all and loves them alike.
doha pls: we're all just humans, why make a fuss about caste
human brotherhood
doha pls: prayer beads in anyone's hand are the same beads, and sand is the same under every foot, no one is higher
The prayer beads are the same in the learned man's hand and the labourer's; the sand beneath both is the same.
My grandmother lent her prayer beads to a washerwoman who came crying to our gate, saying prayer has no caste; make a doha out of her words, and mention the sand on the road.
prayer beads, sand, all equal
Compose a doha that says the prayer beads of the high-born and the low-born are of the same wood, and the sand beneath the feet of both is the same, so devotion cannot be owned by any caste.
At the community kitchen, everyone sits on the floor in the same row and eats the same food, including the collector and the cobbler; I'd love a doha about it.
doha pls: langar-style, everybody eats together, no high and low
same row, same food

Please write a doha that praises the community meal where every person, regardless of caste, wealth or rank, sits side by side, eats the same food, and rises together, showing God's idea of human beings.
Seated in one row on the floor, the lord and the labourer share a single bread.
snake, all equal
Give me a doha that says a snake in the grass does not check a man's caste or purse before it strikes, and in this fear and pain all human beings are the same, so none should look down.
doha pls: a snake bites everyone, and death comes for everyone, nobody's special
A snake once bit the zamindar's son and the servant's son in the same week, and the same village healer cured them both; write a doha about it.
The snake's bite spares not the prince nor the pauper; the poison is one, the pain is one.

Compose a doha that says the lotus rises from the mud and is offered at the shrine without shame, so nobody should be disrespected for the circumstances of his birth, because worth is in what one becomes.
My friend said a lotus grows in the mud and still is loved by all, and he believes no one should be judged by where he was born; please write a doha.
lotus, no birth pride
doha pls: the lotus doesn't care where it grew, people shouldn't either
The lotus blooms from mire into beauty; no one asks it who its parents were.
A thorn in the elephant's foot at the festival made it cry out, and a poor mahout pulled it out with the same hand he would use for a prince's; write a doha.
Please write a doha showing that a thorn hurts the great elephant and the small child in the same way, and that suffering joins high and low, so we should serve each other with equal kindness.
thorn, elephant, same pain
doha pls: an elephant steps on thorns and a king steps on thorns, same pain, same body
The thorn pierces the elephant's foot as it pierces the pauper's; pain is the one language of all creatures.
doha pls: everyone ends in a white shroud, rich or poor, no difference
shroud, same end
My grandfather's shroud was the same plain white as the shroud of his gardener, and the elders said that is how it should be; write a doha about it.
Please craft a couplet that says when the shroud is wrapped around a person, nobody asks whether he was a prince or a pauper, and so we should treat each other now with the same simple respect.
The shroud has no pockets and no rank; it wraps the proud and the humble in the same white.
moneylender, fire, same end

Compose a doha that says the moneylender who counts his coins and the poor man who owes him both warm themselves at the same fire, and the same fire burns them at the last, so pride of wealth is foolish.
doha pls: a moneylender and his debtor both sit by the same fire in the end
The moneylender in our village treated his debtors like dirt, but last winter he sat shivering at the same fire beside them, begging for warmth; I would like a doha on that.
The moneylender's coins and the debtor's rags both feed the same fire at the end; the blaze knows no creditor.
doha pls: the oil press doesn't care whose harvest, it gives the same oil, and the musk deer doesn't choose who to be fragrant for
musk deer, oil press
The oil press crushes the harvest of the rich man's field and the poor man's, and the oil is the same; the musk deer carries its fragrance without asking who will smell it.

The oil press near our village turns out the same pure oil for the landlord and the labourer, and the old pressman, who smells like a musk deer from his herbs, says all are customers of God; write a doha.

Write a doha that says the oil press gives the same oil no matter whose harvest it presses, and the musk deer gives its scent to all who pass, teaching that real worth is shared with everyone equally.
I want a doha that says humans are all made of the same substance and the same breath, that no title, wealth or skin can make one soul better than another, and that kindness is the only true height.
The Maker makes no mistakes in His making; each life is as precious as the next.
equal in creation
doha pls on how we're all equal in the eyes of God
My teacher once made the whole class stand in a line to show that, when we all stand, no one is taller by birth; I'd like a doha based on that.
My mother sat at the spinning wheel every morning in the first sun and spun for any family that needed it, whether high or low, and I'd like a doha that honours her.
sun, spinning wheel, all equal
The sun rises on mansion and hut alike, and the spinning wheel hums the same song for all.

Make me a doha that says the sun gives its warmth to the rich and the poor in the same measure, and the spinning wheel makes yarn for any hand that asks, showing that the Maker gives without choosing.
doha pls: the sun shines on everyone the same, and the spinning wheel doesn't spin for the rich only
Please compose a doha showing that when the one-string lute sings the song of the Maker, the high and the low listen with the same tears, as every heart is moved by the same truth.
The one-string lute plays the same note for the lord and the poor, and the heart that hears it weeps the same tears.
doha pls: a one-string lute plays the same music for everyone, music has no caste
one-string lute, one tune
The old bard with his one-string lute sang in the zamindar's hall and in the labourers' courtyard with the same love, and when asked why, he said the song has no caste; please write a doha.
At the market I watched the vegetable seller give the same fresh leaf to a rich lady and a poor boy with the same smile; write a doha.

Compose a doha that says the buyer in the market does not receive a different leaf for his rank, and so we should respect one another equally, because in the final market of life all are weighed alike.
market, leaf, same respect
doha pls: a leaf in the market sells for the same price whoever buys it, so should respect
In the market every leaf is weighed alike, and so are souls in the eyes of the Maker.
My uncle plays a one-string lute at the gatherings and draws a pot of water for each person who comes, whoever they are; write a doha for him.
The one-string lute sings and the pot of water cools, for lord and servant with a single grace.
Can you make a doha that says the music of the one-string lute and the cool water of the pot are shared without rank, showing a way of life in which everyone is welcomed to drink and to listen.
doha pls: a one-string lute and a pot of water for everyone, no division
lute, pot of water, everyone

Compose a doha that says cotton from the poor man's field and the rich man's field is equally soft and warm, and the garment made from it keeps out the same cold, so there is nothing worth boasting about.
The cotton blooms white in the field of the rich and the poor, and makes the same warm garment for both.
cotton, same fibre
doha pls: cotton is cotton, whether it's worn by a queen or a farmer, so people are people
My neighbour sells cotton to the weavers who make garments for kings and for villagers, and he says it all comes from the same white flower; write a doha about it.
sword, scales, same justice
Compose a doha showing that a just ruler's sword and scales should not tilt toward the rich or lean against the poor, because in the eyes of the Maker every man stands on the same ground.
doha: the sword of justice and the scales see no caste, no rank
The judge and the offender both stood before the same court, and the sword of the law hung above both equally that day, and the scales did not tip for either; write a doha.
Before the sword and the scales, the king and the commoner stand alike; justice has no favourite.
tree, leaf, one root
doha pls: leaves on the same tree are different but they share the same root, people too
In our courtyard the old tree had leaves of every size, and as kids we used to say the big ones were better, until my grandmother told us they all came from one root; write a doha.
Every leaf on the tree is different, yet each drinks from the same root; so are we, children of one.
Pen a doha saying that the leaves of one tree differ in size and shade, but each draws life from the same root and falls the same way, so people of different castes and ranks are of one origin.
The sun burns on all, the pot of water cools all; neither asks for a name.
In the heat of summer, the pot of water by the road was used by farmers and officers alike, and nobody asked who touched it; write a doha about the sun and the pot.

Please write a doha that says the sun shines on all heads and the pot of water by the road quenches every thirst, and so should the human heart give without checking the caste of the person who receives.
doha pls: the sun shines and a pot of water cools anyone, they don't ask caste
pot of water, sun
everyone is the same
I want a doha saying that rank and caste are ideas that humans invented late in the story, that the Maker never wrote them into any heart, and that the true saint looks upon everyone as his own.
doha pls: no one is better than anyone else
In the Maker's eye there is no crown and no rag; every soul is a ray of the same light.
I stopped asking people their surname at work because I realised it didn't change anything about who they are; write a doha.
doha pls: the lotus and sandalwood treat everyone with the same fragrance, so should we
The lotus opens for every eye, the sandalwood scents every hand; so should the heart be for all.
lotus, sandalwood, equal love
My grandmother planted a lotus pond and a sandalwood by the gate, and she let every child, of any caste, pick the flowers and smell the wood; make a doha for her.

Write a doha that says the lotus gives its beauty and sandalwood gives its fragrance to every person without discrimination, so a good human being should give his love and kindness to all with the same generosity.
I want a doha for my school assembly, saying that the Maker made all humans from the same breath and the same light, and anyone who builds walls between persons is going against the Maker's wish.
doha pls: caste is man-made, God never made it
no caste, no rank
Who made the barrier that divides the high from the low? Not the Maker; man alone has made it.
A boy in my class was banned from the shrine because of his birth, and I felt ashamed; I need a doha for this.
doha pls: the winnowing fan blows away the chaff regardless of the farmer's caste
Compose a doha showing that the winnowing fan treats every harvest the same, and in the same way the Maker sifts every soul by its goodness, not by the family or the title it was born with.
At my village's harvest, the upper-caste farmer and the labourer both used the winnowing fan the same way, and the wind blew away chaff from both; write a doha.
The winnowing fan lifts the husk from every farmer's grain, and the wind asks no one's name.
winnowing fan, no caste
cotton, one humanity
Write a doha that says the cotton woven into garments warms every body alike, and the cold wind blows on every shoulder in the same way, so human beings should see each other as the same.
The weaver sells cotton garments to rich and poor, to Hindu and Muslim, with the same measure, and says he sees only customers, not castes; write a doha.
The cotton warms the king and the commoner in the same way, for the cold knows no title.
doha pls: cotton keeps everyone warm, doesn't matter who you are
My mother taught me to call the sweeper "uncle" and the banker "uncle," because she said both are family; write a doha.
I want a doha showing that if you remove names, dress, castes and dwellings from all persons, every soul stands the same before the Maker, and the one who sees this attains peace.
One breath animates the king and the cobbler; one earth receives them both.
doha pls on how everyone is basically the same
same breath
I'd like a doha that says the furnace melts all metals in the same way and the bell rings for every ear, and so the Maker's justice treats all souls alike without regard for rank.
At the blacksmith's furnace, iron from a rich man's and a poor man's cart melted into the same molten red, and the bell nearby rang for both; write a doha.
The furnace melts the blade of the warrior and the plough of the farmer alike, and the bell tolls for both.
furnace, bell, same fate
doha plz: a furnace melts everything alike, and a bell rings the same note for everybody
When my boss treated the cleaner as an equal in front of the whole team, I realised that this is what greatness looks like; write a doha.

Please write a doha that says the only difference between persons is the difference of their deeds, and neither caste nor family nor wealth makes a man great, so we should honour the humble as we honour the powerful.
doha pls on treating everyone equally
Under the same sky we breathe, under the same ground we rest; why then the high and the low?
equal souls
In the forest every plant drinks the same rain, and none is told that it is lesser.
I walked through a forest where a tall teak and a tiny shrub grew side by side, and the guide said they both belonged to the same earth; write a doha.
Write a doha saying that in the forest the great and the small grow in the same soil and under the same sky, and the forest makes no difference between them, and human beings should be the same.
doha pls: in the forest everything grows together, no one asks which is higher caste
forest, equal growth
doha pls: the net of death catches everyone, no one can escape, so no pride
Cast over the whole world is the net of the Maker; all of us are held within it as one.
Give me a doha that says the net of fate falls on all human beings equally, whether king or clerk, and so nobody has the right to boast of rank when bound in the same net as everyone else.
The fisherman casts his net into the waters and it catches every creature alike, the big and the small, and it struck me that death does too; write a doha.
net, same fate
all are one
Heaven is not divided between the rich and the poor; neither is the heart of the Maker.
I want a doha that says the person who respects only the rich and looks down on the poor has not seen the Maker, because the Maker lives equally in the hearts of all His creatures.
At my sister's wedding I watched the groom's family insult the cook, and I felt something break inside; I need a doha for that moment.
doha pls: stop treating people differently by their status
moth, forest, same end
Write a doha saying that in the forest the tiny moth and the towering timber share the same earth in the end, and the human being should learn that no one is high and no one is low.
doha pls: a moth in the forest dies the same as any beast, everyone dies the same, no high and low
I found a dead moth at the foot of a forest giant and thought, both will become the same soil; write a doha.
The moth and the great giants of the forest both return to the same earth; who then is great?
